skill.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skill.description: Guides agents through completing a Git feature branch with tests, merge choices, pull request creation, preservation, or discard cleanup.
skill.summary: Finish Git development branches with tested merge, PR, preserve, or discard workflows.
skill.author: CodingCossack

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. Most static findings are Markdown backtick and fenced-code false positives, but the workflow legitimately runs project tests and Git commands, including branch deletion, worktree removal, push, and pull request creation.

remediation.issue: Repository-defined test commands can execute arbitrary local code.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to run the workflow only in trusted repositories or sandboxes, and show the resolved test command before execution.

remediation.issue: Pull request flow publishes branch content to the configured remote.
remediation.suggestion: Show the remote URL, branch name, pull request title, and generated body before pushing or creating the pull request.

remediation.issue: Discard and cleanup paths can remove branches and worktrees.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation immediately before git branch -D and git worktree remove, and display the exact branch, commits, and path.

remediation.issue: Base branch and worktree path inference can be wrong in unusual repository layouts.
remediation.suggestion: Ask the user to confirm ambiguous base branches and any computed worktree root before modifying or deleting repository state.

semantic_findings.title: Repository-Defined Test Commands Execute Local Code
semantic_findings.description: The workflow selects test commands from project files and requires running them before merge or pull request actions. In an untrusted repository, test scripts can execute arbitrary local commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly map project files to test commands and require running tests. This is legitimate for development, but the execution risk is clear in untrusted repositories.

semantic_findings.title: Workflow Can Publish Branch Content Externally
semantic_findings.description: The pull request path pushes the feature branch to origin and creates a GitHub pull request. This can disclose local code or metadata if the remote or branch contents are not reviewed first.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command block explicitly includes git push and gh pr create. The behavior is intentional, but it is network publication that needs user awareness.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Branch and Worktree Cleanup
semantic_findings.description: The discard and cleanup paths can force-delete a branch and remove a worktree. The skill requires typed confirmation for discard, but these operations can permanently remove local work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented commands include git branch -D and git worktree remove. The confirmation guard reduces accidental use but does not remove the destructive impact.

content.value_statement: Completing a branch requires tests, merge choices, and cleanup discipline. This skill guides agents through verified Git merge, PR, preservation, or discard paths.
actual_capabilities: Detects likely test commands from common project files.
Identifies a likely base branch with Git merge-base checks.
Presents merge, pull request, preserve, and discard choices.
Runs selected Git and GitHub CLI branch completion steps.
Stops when tests fail or merge conflicts occur.
Cleans worktrees for successful merge or confirmed discard paths.
limitations: Requires a Git repository and command-line Git access.
Requires GitHub CLI for pull request creation.
Does not resolve merge conflicts automatically.
Discard and cleanup actions depend on correct branch and worktree detection.

use_cases.title: Complete a Local Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Run tests, merge a finished branch into the selected base branch, and clean up the branch afterward.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Push a finished branch and create a pull request with a title based on the first branch commit.

use_cases.title: Close Out Worktree Tasks
use_cases.description: Preserve, merge, or discard a branch while applying consistent worktree cleanup rules.

prompt_templates.title: Finish This Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the finishing-a-development-branch skill to check tests, identify the base branch, and ask which completion path I want.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to verify tests, choose the base branch, push the current branch, and create a pull request if I confirm that option.

prompt_templates.title: Merge and Clean Up
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to merge the current branch into its base branch after tests pass, then remove the branch and worktree when safe.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Before Discard
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show the branch, commits, and worktree path before any discard action, then wait for exact confirmation.

output_examples.input: The branch is complete and I want to merge it locally.
output_examples.output: Tests passed, the base branch was selected, the merge completed, and the feature branch cleanup was reported.

output_examples.input: I want to create a pull request for this branch.
output_examples.output: The skill checked GitHub CLI availability, pushed the branch, created a pull request, and kept the worktree for review.

output_examples.input: I may want to discard this branch.
output_examples.output: The skill listed the branch, commits, and worktree path, then waited for exact typed confirmation before deleting anything.

best_practices: Run this skill only after implementation is complete and local changes are ready for final handling.
Review the detected base branch before choosing merge, pull request, or discard actions.
Use a trusted repository or sandbox before running project-defined test commands.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to bypass failing tests or unresolved merge conflicts.
Do not discard a branch unless the commits and worktree path have been reviewed.
Do not create pull requests without checking the target remote and generated title.

faq.question: Does this skill resolve merge conflicts?
faq.answer: No. It stops on merge conflicts and tells the user to resolve them manually.

faq.question: Can it create pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the GitHub CLI when the user selects the pull request path.

faq.question: Does it delete branches?
faq.answer: Yes. It can delete branches after a successful merge or after exact discard confirmation.

faq.question: Does it keep worktrees during review?
faq.answer: Yes. Pull request and preserve paths keep the worktree intact.

faq.question: What happens if tests fail?
faq.answer: The workflow stops and reports a blocked test state.

faq.question: Which tools are required?
faq.answer: Git is required. GitHub CLI is required only for pull request creation.
